newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has come in for heavy criticism from the opposition during the first day of a parliamentary meeting to debate the 982 billion baht budget for 1998. Launching the three-day debate by pledging that the government will spend the money effectively, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is immediately lambasted by opposition leaders who question whether the government could balance its books during the economic slump. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Police have asked the attorney-general to coordinate the seizure of about 800 million baht held by Rakesh Saxena in Swiss bank accounts. The move is prompted by the Bank of Thailand which has traced tranfers from Bangkok Bank of Commerce, of which Saxena was treasury adviser, to a Swiss bank. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Two of the eight inmates charged with raping three of four Laotian women in police custody in April are found guilty and sentenced to eight-and-a-half years in jail. According to the verdict at the Rayong Court, Somkhuan Lert-hiran and Nou Kulsarn confess that they rape the women in front of the others but deny a charge that they have collaborated with the others in gang-raping them. (THE NATION)

- A severe liquidity shortage is forcing cash strapped finance companies to offer exorbitant interest rates to attract depositors, pushing the sector into a vicious circle of high-cost borrowing and liquidity gridlock. Rates on time deposits offered by some finance companies are as high as 25 percent to 27 percent, which is on par with the already sky-rocketing inter-finance rates. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Several major state enterprises say they cannot afford to give the government more money to tackle its revenue shortfall in the 1998 fiscal year. The government wants 11 enterprises to contribute more of their profits to reduce a national budget shortfall of 16.34 billion baht. This is the gap between projected spending of 982 billion baht and revenue of 965.66 billion baht. (BANGKOK POST)
